source_text: Still, I think we have now hardened futon1b a good amount if we can do 6m24s of paged queries without setting off alarm bells.  I guess we're pretty much ready, in this case, to do the Minard analysis on the full window?

I guess we're pretty much ready, in this case, to do the Minard analysis on the full window?

reply_text:
㊥ Gist: Almost. Fetching the data for 21 September to today is now low-risk, because the extraction script already takes `--since` and `--before`. The fetch is the smaller part of the job, though. The main work is hand-reading every pattern retrieved since 21 September that isn't among the 689 already labelled. I'd do it in two steps: run the fetch and count the unlabelled patterns, then label them in packs. Shall I send step one to a Kimi or Zai seat?

㊟ (on "without alarm bells") Today I measured single pages, at 0.07–0.40 s each. I have no record of how futon1b behaved during the 6m24s run on 21 September; the method note says only that it paged with `limit=1000` and made no deep health query. It's probably fine, but I haven't checked it. Step one will record futon1b's heap and query slots before and after the fetch, so we'll know.

㊩ (what the extension needs besides the fetch)
- **New patterns to label:** each turn's stage comes from a hand label on the pattern it retrieved. On the 21 September re-run, 94 newly retrieved patterns had to be read by hand. Ten days of new work, covering 象, the Morning Brief and the War Machine contract, will add more. I don't know how many until the fetch has run.
- **Your-turn count:** before 27 September, park wake-ups were filed as your turns. The Minard filter removes resume markers by their text, but it predates some wake formats. Step one should also run `xiang2000_p6o3.classify`, the filter I used today, and report any turns where the two filters disagree.
- **Token panel:** the figure's lower panel comes from a separate report of Codex token use in the gaps between your turns. That report would need regenerating to cover the new dates. Without it, the figure for the new dates has only its upper panel.
- **Hard-coded dates:** `minard_operator_work.py` has its start and end dates written in. That's a small edit.

㭭 (order)
1. **Fetch and count** (Kimi or Zai): run `pattern_stage_evidence.py --fetch --since 2026-09-21T17:19:12.718167Z` up to now, then report:
   - turn and retrieval counts;
   - join outcomes;
   - the list of rank-one pattern IDs with no label yet;
   - futon1b heap before and after.
2. **Label** the new IDs in packs of about ten, using the existing rubric. Each label quotes the pattern source, as the current EDN does.
3. **Rebuild** the stage table and the figure for 22 August to today.

Once the 象 backfill finishes, the PBASE comparison can use this extended set.

🈸 (one decision) Shall I dispatch step 1? Reply `yes` to proceed.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: Gist: Reading and analysing your roughly 5,000 turns doesn't load futon1b at all. The 象 readers work from turn files already on disk and write their readings to disk too, so the store is only touched when the turns are first harvested, which takes a few seconds in pages. The cases that have actually hurt futon1b are different ones: bulk writes, and one unbounded deep health check.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(what I measured this turn)
- **Paged reads:** a page of 1,000 of your turns took 0.07–0.40 s, about 2 MB each. Today's harvests were 4 pages for your turns since 21 September and 7 for the start records. Neither caused trouble.
- **Memory:** futon1b's heap is at 2.7 of 4 GB. Its health page shows a concurrency limit, with 2 query slots free when I looked.
- **The backfill itself:** `backfill_pack.py` and `session_turn_analysis.py` contain no network calls. The packs are built from the turn files under `storage/operator-turns/`, and the readings are written back there. So the four seats reading now cost the Kimi and Codex seats their time, not futon1b.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(what is still unsafe)
- **Bulk writes:** about 330 mission-file rewrites on 30 September set off around 9 times as many store writes. That led to timeouts and a nearly full heap, and every Agency job was blocked while the store was busy.
- **Deep health check:** `/health?deep=true` pushed a nearly full heap into an out-of-memory exit on 23 August.
- **Unpaged queries:** the entities endpoint stops at 5,000 rows and offers no way to page past that. A query without `limit` or a date range asks the store for far more than it needs.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (why the Minard extraction was slower) It took 6m24s because it pulled every pattern retrieval in the window, 20,306 rows over 21 pages, as well as 5,786 rows of your turns. That still means a few minutes of paged reads, not a load that stops the store working. The comparison job that's on hold would read the Minard results and the 象 readings from disk, so it needn't query futon1b at all.
